To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the polarization of the secondary protons from quasielastic (p2p) scattering of 1 GeV protons on 14He is less than that of the protons in free proton-proton elastic scattering.

the polarization of the secondary proton in the quasielastic (p2p) scattering from 4He is less than that of free elastic proton-protons, and the magnitude of this difference depends on the binding energy of the s-shell protons, but does not depend on the effective density of the nucleus.

the polarization of secondary proton in the (p,2) scattering on a He nucleus at 1-GeV is less than that of free proton-proton scattering, and that this difference is determined mainly by the mean binding energies of s-shell proton in the He nucleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the polarization of protons scattered from the 4He nucleus in the kinematic region of the quasielastic reaction (p, 1p) and the elastic reaction (p, p).
the investigation of polarization phenomena in the quasielastic (p,pn) reaction on a 4 He nucleus at 1-GeV.
a detailed study of quasielastic and elastic proton-nucleus scattering at 1 Gev.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the polarization of the scattered proton is less than the polarization of the proton in free elastic scattering, the difference being determined mainly by the mean binding energies of the s-shell protons.
the polarization of secondary proons is less in quasielastic than in elastic scattering of 2 GeV protons on 12C.
the polarization of the secondary proton is determined by the binding energy of the proton, and not by the effective nuclear radius.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the polarization in the inclusive quasielastic scattering of 1 GeV protons on 12C and 4He nuclei is determined by the effective nuclear potential rather than by the mean binding energies of the s-shell protons.
polarization in quasielastic proton-nucleus scattering is determined not only by the effective nuclear densities but also by the mean binding energies of s-shell nucleons.

the polarization of secondary proons from quasielastic scattering is less than that from elastic scattering and that this difference is determined not by the effective nuclear densities but by the binding energies of s-shell proons in nuclei.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polarization of secondary proton in the (p,2P) reaction on 4He nucleus is less than that of free p-p elastic scattering.
the polarization transfer in the quasi-elastic scattering of protons from the 4He nuclei at 1 Gev is less than in the elastic scattering.
the polarization of secondary proton in quasielastic scattering of 1 GeV protons on 12C nucleus is less than that of elastic scattering.
